### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/client`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **82** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-mcp-access-token.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**61** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 90523379a149e85afa1ed49286a3abaa95075c42`.

⛔ **12** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-mcp-access-token.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `userId (5 routes)`
- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `created_at (literal, 43 pages)`, `sys_user (literal, 49 pages)`
- **12** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **224** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **161** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **161**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **57** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **38** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 90523379a149e85afa1ed49286a3abaa95075c42` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6c77ed5a8d4195c6d19d66245df8a6cca2b1c95e` — the merge of head `618a9fb2c3801011ccd36c5fa21aecd0e189a505` into base `90523379a149e85afa1ed49286a3abaa95075c42`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6c77ed5a8d4195c6d19d66245df8a6cca2b1c95e && git checkout 6c77ed5a8d4195c6d19d66245df8a6cca2b1c95e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 90523379a149e85afa1ed49286a3abaa95075c42 618a9fb2c3801011ccd36c5fa21aecd0e189a505 && git checkout -B drift-repro 90523379a149e85afa1ed49286a3abaa95075c42 && git merge --no-ff 618a9fb2c3801011ccd36c5fa21aecd0e189a505

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 90523379a149e85afa1ed49286a3abaa95075c42
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 90523379a149e85afa1ed49286a3abaa95075c42` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

`@better-auth/oauth-provider` 1.7.12 consent endpoints, PR #30879 at `36d3a9fd823694d741e71173b38c783753ffdaaf` (its `auth-manager.ts`, `auth-manager-mcp-access-token.ts`, `auth-manager-request-routing.ts`, `mcp-token-revocation.ts`)

Reviewed against the merge base with `origin/main`, `4d56914aaa8c2cf388986309364eef23eea10282`: 24 files, +1874 / -31. The head did not move during this review. Nothing was built, run or re-run; the one local operation beyond reading was a `git merge-tree` of this head against #30879's head, which is a diff computation, not a run.

The recogniser (`record-recognisers.mjs --template --paths ...`) says the changed paths decide no face on their own and the changesets' `Clause-②: yes (widening)` line maps to the declaration face (`TIER_DEFAULT`). This record is served at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` because the claim (6683953156) and the seat's order owe one for a security-labelled access boundary; the owed tier is a floor, not an exact match (contract-review.md, "档恰等不作下限"). The seat should keep the two in view when it writes the ACCEPT.

### ① Derived judgments

**Must-fix: none.**

**Should-fix (none blocks the verdict; each is small and named with its line):**

1. `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/mcp-client-last-use.ts:205-213`: the stamper reports only the FIRST failure in the process and then goes silent forever (`failureReported`). A benign race can consume that one report: the token verifies while the consent still exists, the person withdraws the consent before the after-response task runs, and `stamp(consent.id, ...)` then updates a row that is gone. If the engine rejects that update, the one error line in this process is spent on a race, and a later real outage (the missing column, an unreachable store) is never reported. Suggested fix: report once per DISTINCT error message, or treat a not-found on the update as a no-op before the catch. Not a security defect; an observability gap.
2. `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/authorized-clients-read.ts:206-217` (`scopesOf`): one consent row whose `scopes` text does not decode makes the whole read answer `500` for that person, on both doors. The module says this is deliberate ("refused loudly rather than answered as a grant of nothing"). It is a reasonable choice, but a single corrupt row then hides every other grant from the person and from the administrator. Consider answering the bad row with `scopes: []` plus a logged error, or skipping it with a log line, so one row cannot blank the list. Not a security defect.
3. The dev report's summary says "at most once per consent per hour". The code (`mcp-client-last-use.ts:45-50, 186-204`) makes that true per PROCESS: each process reads once per consent per hour, and the first calls of an hour in several processes can each write the same hour start. The PR body says this honestly ("or a few times with the same value when first calls race"). The card's requirement is "no per-request write storm, a coarse timestamp is enough", which is met. The ledger note and changeset wording ("at most once per consent per hour") should say "per process", or the seat should accept the PR body's fuller wording as the one of record.
4. `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/authorized-clients-read.real-plugin.test.ts:453-477` (rule 7): the refused callers are a member with no organization, the OWNER and the ADMIN of an organization the target is in, and the target themself. There is no explicit case for an organization admin of an organization the target is NOT in. The gate reads no organization at all (`platform-admin-gate.ts:176-213`), so the case is covered by construction, but rule 7's "outside their organizations" clause would be cheap to pin with one more sign-up.
5. Acknowledged by the dev, outside this card's surface, owed a follow-up card: a banned subject's verified token still stamps `last_used_at`, because the ban read runs after `verifyMcpAccessToken` in `packages/runtime/src/security/resolve-execution-context.ts:200-208`. The stamp then records an hour in which the MCP door refused the call. Rule 6 says "recorded only on a verified MCP call"; the token verified, the call did not run. An administrator reading the list would see a banned person's assistant as "used" at that hour. The seat should file it rather than leave it in Acceptance notes.

**Confirmed, by file:line.**

Own read (rule 1):
- Subject comes from the session only: `authorized-clients-read.ts:325-328` reads `deps.readCallerSession(request.headers)` and takes `session.user.id`; nothing from the query or body reaches `readAuthorizedClients(deps, subject)` at `:336`. The session read is better-auth's own `getSession` with `inProcessSessionReadInput(headers)` (`:235-238`).
- Closed empty query set: `AUTHORIZED_CLIENTS_QUERY_PARAMS` is a frozen empty array (`:103`); `unknownQueryParamRefusalMessage` (`packages/rest/src/query-allowlist.ts:185-196`) refuses ANY key, including `userId`, with `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`authorized-clients-read.ts:333-334`). Hono's `c.req.queries()` gives `{ userId: [''] }` for `?userId=`, so the empty-valued spelling is refused too. A parameter is refused, never ignored: the card's rule 1 and the dev's claim hold.
- Order: 401 (`:328`), held-session 403 (`:330-331`), 400 on a parameter (`:333-334`), then the read. An anonymous caller is answered 401 before any query is read.

Admin read (rules 2, 3, 4):
- Gate before query: `auth-plugin.ts:3816-3820` runs `gateAdmin(c)` and returns its Response before the handler module is even imported; the query is read only inside `runAdminAuthorizedClientsRead` (`authorized-clients-read.ts:349-362`). `gateAdmin` (`auth-plugin.ts:3602-3615`) reads the session from headers and calls `judgePlatformAdmin`, the same judge `sys-session/revoke` uses (`sys-session-revoke.ts:281`).
- Byte-identical 403: `judgePlatformAdmin` (`platform-admin-gate.ts:176-213`) answers 401 `UNAUTHENTICATED` for no session, then the held-session refusal, then 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` with the constant `PLATFORM_ADMIN_REFUSAL_MESSAGES[403]`. The verdict depends on the caller's session alone, never on `userId` or on whether the target exists. The test pins the text equal across existing id, nonexistent id and no id for member, org owner, org admin and self (`authorized-clients-read.real-plugin.test.ts:463-476`).
- Reach: `isPlatformAdminUser` is the ADR-0068 D2 standing (the `admin_full_access` permission set in the test fixture, `:114-125`). Organization owners and admins are not platform admins and are refused (test `:456-462` with `isPlatformAdmin` precondition false at `:464`).
- Per organization: every row carries `organizationId` from the consent's `reference_id` (`authorized-clients-read.ts:258, :313`); the test pins a person's grants across two organizations plus one with none (`:436-451`). The platform admin's reach across the tenant wall on a better-auth-managed object is ADR-0095 D1 (`docs/adr/0095-...md:130-134`).
- Read only (rule 4): the only mount is `rawApp.get` (`auth-plugin.ts:3816`); there is no withdraw path in the module. The consent `id` the admin door hands out cannot be turned into a withdrawal of another person's grant: the installed provider's `deleteConsentEndpoint` and `updateConsentEndpoint` (1.7.12, `dist/authorize-D_jy3s-1.mjs:3141-3176`) both refuse unless `consent.userId === session.user.id`. So no widening leaks through the id.
- Past the gate: missing, empty, whitespace, repeated and unknown parameters are 400 (`authorized-clients-read.ts:349-362`); an id naming no user is 404 (`:363-365`, `userExists` at `:280-285`). The 404 is answered only to a platform admin, who can already list users.

No credential material (rule 5):
- The consent read names its columns: `['id','client_id','reference_id','scopes','created_at','last_used_at']` (`authorized-clients-read.ts:245`); the client read names `['client_id','name']` only (`:269`); the user read names `['id']` (`:282`). No token, code, secret or session column is ever loaded.
- Each answered row is built from exactly seven members (`:308-316`); the test pins the exact key set (`ROW_KEYS`, test `:64, :362, :449`) and that the client secret, an access token, a refresh token and every `sys_session.token` are absent from the response text (`:254-262`).
- Refusals carry only code and message (`:289-297`); the 500 path answers a fixed message and logs the error server-side (`auth-plugin.ts:3825-3829, :4665-4669`). The only id that can appear in a logged error is a consent id (`scopesOf`, `:216`), not token material.
- `Cache-Control: no-store` on every answer (`:183, :296, :317`).

Last-use stamp (rule 6):
- Written only after a verified token: `auth-manager.ts:4445-4448` attaches `.then` to the verifier's promise and calls `scheduleMcpClientLastUse(principal)` only when a principal came back. The principal's `userId`, `clientId` (`azp`) and `organizationId` are read from the verified JWT (`auth-manager-mcp-access-token.ts`), never from a request field; a token with no `azp` stamps nothing (`auth-manager.ts:4464`, `mcp-client-last-use.ts:188`).
- Keyed to the right consent: `consentsFor(clientId, userId)` reads `where: { client_id, user_id }` (`mcp-client-last-use.ts:140-150`) and `consentForToken` picks the row whose `reference_id` equals the token's organization claim, or the row with none (`:99-106`). That is the provider's `findConsent` rule and matches #30879's `isConsentFor` (`mcp-token-revocation.ts:147-149`). The test pins that a token for organization A stamps only the A consent and a token with no claim stamps only the no-organization consent (`mcp-client-last-use.real-engine.test.ts:240-259`).
- Coarse and rate-limited: the value is the hour start (`:109-111, :204`); a row is written only when its stored hour is older (`:203`); a per-process memo skips every later call of the hour (`:190-195`), claimed before the I/O and kept on failure. Across processes: each reads once per hour; a process whose clock lags cannot overwrite a newer stamp, because the row is left alone whenever its stored hour is not older than the current one (`:203`). The test counts engine reads and writes: 25 calls in one hour give 1 read and 1 write; a second manager on the same store gives 1 read and 0 writes (`test:181-238`).
- Off the request path: `runAfterResponse` (`run-after-response.ts:35-47`) schedules with `setImmediate`, never awaited; `record` never rejects (`mcp-client-last-use.ts:205-213`); the `.then` returns the principal unchanged. The test pins a store that throws on every write: every verdict still answered, 2 attempts over two hours, 1 error report naming the column (`test:354-384`).
- The only caller: `verifyMcpAccessToken` is called from `packages/runtime/src/security/resolve-execution-context.ts:200` and only when `acceptOAuthAccessToken` is set, which only `packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts:753` sets, for `/mcp` paths. No REST or GraphQL call can produce a stamp. #30879's `/oauth2/revoke` uses `verifyMcpAccessTokenClaims` directly, not the manager method, so a revoke does not stamp.
- Not settable through any consent door: the provider's `update-consent` body is `z.object({ id, update: z.object({ scopes }) })` (1.7.12, `dist/authorize-D_jy3s-1.mjs:3219-3229`), so `lastUsedAt` and `last_used_at` are stripped at the top level and inside `update`; the real-engine test posts both spellings in both places and reads the stamp back as null while the scopes moved (`test:300-351`). The object is `apiEnabled: false` (`sys-oauth-consent.object.ts:141`), so no data-API write reaches the column, and the parity pin (`oauth-provider-schema-parity.test.ts:92-101`) fails if a provider bump ever declares a consent field that lands on `last_used_at`.
- System-context write: `mcp-client-last-use.ts:113, :158` writes under `isSystem: true`. Justified: the object is `managedBy: 'better-auth'`, and ADR-0092 D2 says only internal writes bypass the identity write guard (`identity-write-guard.ts:96-99`, `docs/adr/0092-...md:29-35`); a user-context write would be refused by design. The write is censused: the regenerated ledger row `mcp-client-last-use.ts | update | sys_oauth_consent | enabled | elevated | 1` (`docs/audits/2026-08-tenant-audit-write-call-sites.counts.md:156`) and the counts 261 to 262.

Ledger, client, object, dogfood:
- Two `AUTH_ROUTE_LEDGER` rows, `family: 'objectstack-mount'`, `source: 'objectstack'`, `disposition: 'sdk'`, `client:` naming the two SDK methods; the tracker id is in the comment, not the `note` (`auth-route-ledger.ts:191-199`). The conformance own-list pin adds both routes in sorted position (`auth-route-ledger.conformance.test.ts:223-236`), and the `live.has(route)` loop holds them to the live mount.
- `packages/client/src/index.ts:1242-1270` exports `AuthorizedClient` and `AuthorizedClientsList`; `:4999-5031` adds `oauth.authorizedClients.list()` (sends no parameter) and `.listForUser(userId)` (encodes the id). Both unwrap the envelope and throw on a refusal (test `:38-71`). `auth-route-ledger-coverage.test.ts:57` and `client-url-conformance.test.ts:121` derive from the ledger, so the new `client:` names are driven.
- `last_used_at` is `Field.datetime({ required: false, readonly: true })` (`sys-oauth-consent.object.ts:124-130`), with a comment naming its one writer. Four translation bundles carry the label and help, the three non-English ones hand-written and faithful to the English.
- Dogfood: `objectstack-gate` row with `query` (`admin-route-nonadmin-refusal.dogfood.test.ts:286-291`; `RouteExpectation.query` exists at `:196`) and the `ADMITTED` row plus a `bodies` query entry (`admin-platform-admin-standing.dogfood.test.ts:244-248, :718-721`). Without the query the admin answer would be 400 past the gate, which `diedBeforeTheGate` (`:771-777`) reads as a void measurement, so the entry is part of the classification, as the dev says.

**Rule-by-rule (security#1, 6683642288):**

1. Own read keyed by the session subject only; a selector is refused, not ignored. MET: `authorized-clients-read.ts:103, :325-336`; test `:372-394`.
2. Admin read as a separate door, same gate and reach as the admin session doors, never wider; same refusal whether or not the target exists. MET under the dev's reading A (judgePlatformAdmin, the gate of `sys-session/revoke`; `auth-plugin.ts:3815`, `platform-admin-gate.ts:176-213`); test `:453-477`. The reading itself is OWED security#1's confirmation (③).
3. Per organization; an administrator sees grants only inside their reach. MET under reading A: a platform admin's reach is every organization (ADR-0095 D1), and every row names its `organizationId` (`:313`); test `:436-451`. Owed security#1's confirmation of the reading (③).
4. Read only; no admin withdrawal. MET: a GET-only mount, no withdraw path; the provider's own consent doors bind the id to the session user (`dist:3154, :3176`).
5. No credential material. MET: named columns only (`:245, :269, :282`), seven fixed members (`:308-316`); test `:254-262, :362-363, :449-450`.
6. Last use server-written, only on a verified MCP call, coarse, nothing a client sends sets it. MET: `auth-manager.ts:4445-4448, :4464`, `mcp-client-last-use.ts:99-111, :186-204`, the MCP-only caller (`resolve-execution-context.ts:200`, `http-dispatcher.ts:753`), the provider's zod body (`dist:3222-3225`), `apiEnabled: false`; real-engine test `:262-351`. One caveat in should-fix 5 (a banned subject's refused call still stamps).
7. Tests on the real plugin, in addition to the card's three: a member naming another's id refused; an admin refused outside reach and outside their organizations; no token material. MET: real AuthManager, real AuthPlugin routes, consents written through better-auth's adapter (`test:1-25, :216-246`); member `?userId=` 400 with none of the other's rows (`:372-384`); org owner and org admin of the target's organization refused identically (`:453-477`); no token material (`:254-262`). The one gap is should-fix 4 (no explicit org admin of a foreign organization).

**Ablations, as reported (not re-run):** read against the tests, each would go red as described. (1) honouring `userId` on the own read fails `:372-384` and `:386-394`; (1b) dropping the `user_id` filter fails `:348-370` because Alice would see Bob's rows; (2) removing `gateAdmin` fails the anonymous 401 case (`:396-405`) and rule 7 (`:453-477`); (3) a per-call precise write fails every stamp case, since each compares the stored value to the hour start and counts writes; (4) deleting the `ADMITTED` entry trips the standing sweep's first assertion on an unclassified mount.

### ② Semver level

Three `patch` changesets, each carrying `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` as line-initial declarations; the PR body carries the same two lines. Per AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3, the level follows the Metadata-protocol kind alone: `none` takes `patch`, and a widening that is not a protocol change ships `patch`. Correct.

`Clause-②: yes (widening)` is right: two new served routes in `AUTH_ROUTE_LEDGER`, two new `@objectstack/client` methods and two exported types, one new nullable column on a shipped object, nothing removed or tightened. `Metadata-protocol: none` is defensible and consistent with precedent (platform-objects CHANGELOG, "platform object metadata only, no authorable key"): the object is `lock: 'full'`, `managedBy: 'better-auth'`, `apiEnabled: false`, so no metadata author gains a key, value or type to write; the served meta shape of `sys_oauth_consent` gains one field, which the Clause-② widening line already covers. No `Skills-docs:` line is owed (kind `none`, no narrowing arm). No `packages/spec/**` change, no governed path, no breaking banner needed.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Reading A of rules 2 and 3 is owed security#1's confirmation (6683944651, not yet answered).** The build matches that reading exactly: platform admins only (`judgePlatformAdmin`), across every organization, each row labelled with `organizationId`; organization owners and admins refused byte-identically to a stranger. It admits nobody the card's rules do not: the gate is the one `sys-session/revoke` uses for one person acting on another's sessions, and no organization-admin lane exists.
